to deliver his right hand? And in this year, Nur al-Din went to the territory of Damascus,
and he sent word to the Damascenes:
"I have not come to wage war with you,
but to remove the reproach from you.
For behold, you are subjugated under the tribute of the Franks,
and your sons and your daughters are captives with the Franks,
and they have no helper."
The Damascenes, however, sent back to him:
"We are at peace with the Franks,
and we have no need of your help.
And if you do not leave and return to your own land,
behold, we will send after the Franks to come,
and we together with them will meet you with the sword."
And when Nur al-Din heard an embassy such as this, he was inflamed with wrath,
and he wanted to go and encamp against the city.
Then God sent heavy and pouring rains,
and he was hindered.
And the magnates of Damascus came out to him and pacified him,
and they proclaimed him after the Caliph and Sultan.
And he left them and returned to Aleppo. And in the year
one thousand four hundred and sixty-three {OCR?: 1463}
of the Greeks,
(1152 of our Lord?), again the Franks went forth from Rome in wrath against the deceitful Greeks,
and they came and burned the whole territory of Constantinople.
And they also went forth into Palestine,
and they burned many villages in the territory of Ascalon,
and they shed much blood of the Turks and Arabs whom they found.
And they also went forth into Egypt,
and they destroyed and burned many cities and villages in the west of Egypt,
and they returned to their own land.
And in the same year died Dawlah, the lord of Melitene,
and his son Dhu'l-Qarnayn reigned after him.
And when Mas'ud, the Sultan of Iconium, heard this,
he came against Ya'qub Arslan, the brother of Dawlah.
And when he had subjugated him,
he encamped against Melitene,
and devastated all the orchards around it.
Then the mother of the youth came out to him,
because she was his niece,
and she interceded with him on behalf of her son.
And the Sultan said:
"If he comes out to me and submits,
he will be received by me,
and the city shall remain his."
Then the youth came out,
bearing a sword and a burial shroud.
And he received him,
and confirmed him in the rulership,
and he departed and went away.
Then his mother gained control over the city,
and she inflicted many evils,
not only upon the Christians,
but also upon the Muslims,
especially by levying taxes.
